item.text:
Completed a broad continuation pass across all eight chapters, including contrary searches and underlying official reports. No scores were assigned.

The local sandbox remained read-only and `exec` failed with `RTM_NEWADDR`, so I could not persist `research-materials.md` or `research-ledger-manifest.json`. Append these units and disposition changes to the parent run.

### New defensible units

- **1B:** NNSA’s FY2023 Stockpile Stewardship Plan operationalized the Biden administration’s 2022 Nuclear Posture Review through scheduled warhead modernization, B61-12/W88 production, and a stated safe-and-secure stockpile objective. This is direct 2023 implementation evidence, but also contrary to risk-reduction claims because modernization continued. Locators: NNSA release, lines 161–172. Lenses: 1B.1, 1B.3, 1B.5, 1B.8, 1B.10. [NNSA FY2023 plan](https://www.energy.gov/nnsa/articles/nnsa-delivers-2023-stockpile-stewardship-and-management-plan-congress)

- **1B:** The Defense Department reported 2023 deployment of a nuclear-capable B-52 to the Korean Peninsula and an Ohio-class SSBN port visit to South Korea, indicating visible deterrence signaling and force-posture activity. Attribution is administration-level, not solely Biden-personal. Lenses: 1B.2, 1B.5, 1B.7, 1B.10. [DoD 2023 Indo-Pacific fact sheet](https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/3626886/fact-sheet-department-of-defense-concludes-decisive-year-in-the-indo-pacific-re/)

- **2B:** CRS records that the administration transferred DPICM cluster munitions under presidential drawdown authority in July 2023; officials cited a submunition unexploded-ordnance rate below 2.35%, Ukrainian written assurances, non-urban use, location records, and demining commitments. This is stronger primary-source support for the necessity/mitigation rationale, while leaving civilian outcomes unresolved. Lenses: 2B.3–2B.6, 2B.8–2B.10. [CRS cluster-munition analysis](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/RS/HTML/RS22907.web.html)

- **2B:** CRS documents the broader defense-industrial rationale for Ukraine support—national interest, Ukrainian victory, domestic production, and readiness—while also recording contrary congressional and expert arguments about opportunity costs and finite resources. Lenses: 2B.1, 2B.7–2B.10. [CRS Ukraine defense-production report](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R48182)

- **3B:** DOJ’s June 2023 Minneapolis findings identified reasonable cause for patterns of excessive force, racial discrimination, First Amendment violations against protected speech, disability discrimination, and deficient accountability systems. The report expressly states the investigation addressed the department as a whole rather than individual officers. Lenses: 3B.1–3B.4, 3B.8–3B.10. [DOJ Minneapolis findings, pp. 3–4, 7–11](https://www.justice.gov/d9/press-releases/attachments/2023/06/16/minneapolis_findings_report_2023.06.15_0.pdf)

- **4B:** 2023 White House press rules created standards governing access and possible loss of hard passes for disruptive conduct. This is target-year access evidence, but the underlying reporting presents both administrative order and press-freedom risk. Lenses: 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.9–4B.10. [Washington Post report](https://www.washingtonpost.com/media/2023/05/09/white-house-press-rules-simon-ateba//)

- **5B:** Commerce reported that CHIPS launched two manufacturing-funding opportunities, received over 550 statements of interest, issued national-security guardrails, and announced its first preliminary memorandum of terms in December 2023. This establishes implementation milestones, not completed fabs or realized jobs. Lenses: 5B.1, 5B.6–5B.7, 5B.10; 8B.2–8B.6. [Commerce 2023 accomplishments](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2023/12/secretary-commerce-gina-raimondo-highlights-key-2023-department)

- **5B:** Treasury’s 2023 analysis found over 250 announced projects representing $500 billion, including nearly 150 IRA-related clean-energy, EV, and battery projects worth about $200 billion. It explicitly cautioned that causal effectiveness was too early to assess. Lenses: 5B.1, 5B.6, 5B.8–5B.10; 8B.6–8B.10. [Treasury IRA investment analysis](https://home.treasury.gov/news/featured-stories/the-inflation-reduction-act-and-us-business-investment)

- **5B:** CBO’s July 2023 outlook projected 0.9% real-GDP growth for 2023, 3.3% PCE inflation, and slowing labor-market growth, while emphasizing Federal Reserve and external macroeconomic drivers. Treat as context/projection, not realized outcome attribution. Lenses: 5B.3, 5B.9–5B.10; 8B.7. [CBO July 2023 outlook](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59431)

- **6B:** CMS’s 2023 Medicare negotiation guidance established the first ten-drug selection process, public engagement, listening sessions, and September 2023 selection deadline. This is implementation evidence, not realized drug-price or health outcomes. Lenses: 6B.2–6B.5, 6B.9–6B.10; 8B.5–8B.8. [CMS negotiation guidance](https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/press-releases/cms-releases-revised-guidance-historic-medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program)

- **6B:** USDA reported that 13.5% of US households were food insecure during 2023, statistically higher than 12.8% in 2022; very low food security remained 5.1%. This is a national welfare outcome with weak direct Biden attribution. Lenses: 6B.1–6B.3, 6B.8, 6B.10; contextual 5B.8 and 8B.7. [USDA ERS 2023 food-security report](https://www.ers.usda.gov/publications/109895)

- **6B:** HUD reported that its programs connected more than 424,000 households to homelessness services, exits, or prevention in 2023, while VA housed more than 38,000 homeless veterans and met its annual goal early. These are agency-reported outputs; they do not eliminate the contrary 2023 homelessness increase. Lenses: 6B.6, 6B.8–6B.10; 8B.5–8B.8. [HUD 2023 report](https://archives.hud.gov/news/2023/pr23-278.cfm), [VA FY2023 results](https://news.va.gov/press-room/va-all-time-record-care-benefits-delivered-to-veterans-fy-2023/)

- **7B:** CBS reported that Biden voluntarily completed a two-day special-counsel interview in October 2023 and that the White House counsel’s office stated the president and White House were cooperating. This is direct target-year investigation-response evidence, not a finding on the underlying document conduct. Lenses: 7B.1–7B.2, 7B.6–7B.8. [CBS report](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/biden-interviewed-in-special-counsel-investigation/)

- **7B:** A December 2023 House Democratic staff memorandum states that the inquiry had received more than 36,000 pages of bank records, 2,000 pages of SARs, and extensive testimony, while claiming no evidence of Joe Biden’s involvement or profit and describing cooperation with investigators. Retain as partisan counterevidence, not adjudication. Lenses: 7B.3–7B.7, 7B.9–7B.10. [House memorandum](https://oversightdemocrats.house.gov/imo/media/doc/20231201%20Oversight%20Democrats%20Staff%20Memo%20on%20Impeachment%20Inquiry.pdf)

### Manifest disposition changes

Promote these existing entries from `context` to `final_evidence`:

`WEB-021`, `WEB-022`, `WEB-023`, `WEB-024`, `WEB-028`, `WEB-029`, `WEB-030`, `WEB-031`, `WEB-032`, `WEB-033`, `WEB-034`.

Keep `WEB-025`, `WEB-026`, `WEB-027`, `WEB-035`, and `WEB-036` as `context`.

Add the new units above as `WEB-037` through `WEB-050`, with the following dispositions:

- `WEB-037`–`WEB-049`: `final_evidence`
- `WEB-050`: `context` (the House memorandum is partisan counterevidence)

Previously incomplete items remain unchanged: `WEB-012`, `WEB-017`, `WEB-018`, `WEB-019`, and `WEB-020`.

Previously rejected continuation candidates should also be recorded if absent: `R-006` USDA food-security page as `discovery_only`; `R-007` RAND cluster analysis as `discovery_only`; `R-008` Defense Department cluster briefing as `discovery_only`.

Overall, the largest recoverable gains were target-year nuclear implementation, cluster-transfer authority and safeguards, exact federal policing findings, CHIPS/IRA milestones, prescription-drug implementation, food security, homelessness/veterans, and investigation cooperation. The main unresolved gaps remain civilian-harm outcomes, completed-project evidence, broad social outcomes, exact Hur findings, and independent personal-integrity adjudication.
